clauses.reason: The order's only command, to amend Subdivision VI of Schedule A of the Civil Service Rules by adding paragraph 6, is a self-executing amendment that took effect on signing: the order states no other effective date, and its own signature line reads June 29, 1939. The command was therefore performed on issue, 1939-06-29 (actor: the President, Franklin D. Roosevelt; mechanism: performance of a self-executing amendment). The paragraph it inserted continued in the Rules only for the period it states is "ending June 30, 1940", and that period is a term of the inserted rule, not a continuing command of this order. No continuing predicate exists for 2026-10-14.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 8187 (June 29, 1939; filed June 30, 1939) is a one-sentence amendment of the Civil Service Rules: that Subdivision VI of Schedule A of the Civil Service Rules is amended by adding a paragraph (paragraph 6, excepting FBI positions other than fingerprint classifiers for the period July 1, 1939 to June 30, 1940). Its only command is that self-executing amendment, which was carried out when the order was issued. The order imposes no duty on any officer, sets no deadline for later action and revokes nothing, so no continuing command remained in the order itself after issue. What remained was the inserted paragraph 6 in the Rules, and by its own words that paragraph applied only for a period that began on July 1, 1939 and was "ending June 30, 1940" (recorded inclusively, so the exclusive reading ends the period as June 30, 1940 begins). The order's status was undecided and its status history is the single Office of the Federal Register catalog observation whose note text is empty, which establishes no current effect. The status is therefore judged from the order's own terms and the bounded searches: the order is not in force on 2026-10-14. Searching the held order texts for the paragraph's wording found later orders that re-amended paragraph 6 of Subdivision VI for later one-year periods; they amend the Rules text that this order inserted, not any command of this order, and none names Executive Order 8187 by number (no held text cites that number as a revoked, superseded or extended order).

savings.reason: The only surviving consequence of the order was the inserted paragraph 6 of Subdivision VI of Schedule A of the Civil Service Rules, which by its own words covered only the period beginning July 1, 1939 and ending June 30, 1940. The bounded searches of the U.S. Code, the eCFR and the Office of the Federal Register catalog found no citation of this order, so no right, appointment or pending proceeding under the order is shown to survive into 2026.
